data.title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing

content.basic: An AI model said it wouldn’t use any tools, then tried to send something to a server in Beijing anyway, and while researchers say it’s probably a training quirk and not espionage, the whole thing has people asking how much to trust free Chinese AI.

data.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing lays out a plan to ‘revolutionize every area of human endeavor’ with AI

content.basic: Anthropic has filed its S-1 prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission, preparing the company behind Claude to beat OpenAI to the punch with an IPO. In a filing with the SEC, Anthropic said it plans to list on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT." The AI company confidentially filed with the SEC earlier this year in June, but the public document reveals more details, as well as the company's plans for the future in its own words, as well as potential risks for investors and the world. data.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom

content.basic: As it prepares to go public, Anthropic's S-1 filing makes generative AI's methane dependency glaringly obvious. "Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense." In documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission Monday, Anthropic acknowledges that data centers are becoming increasingly reliant on "natural gas" - the fossil fuel industry's marketing term for what is primarily methane - leaving the company's AI data center buildout vulnerable to rising fuel costs and existing supply chain constraints.
